text: Vietjet named among Việt Nam's 50 best-performing listed companies in 2026

HCM CITY - Vietjet has been named among Việt Nam's 50 best-performing listed companies in 2026, in a ranking compiled by Nhịp Cầu Đầu Tư Magazine, alongside major companies including Vinamilk and FPT.

The ranking, which has been conducted annually since 2012, evaluates listed companies' business performance over three consecutive years based on revenue growth, return on equity (ROE) and earnings per share (EPS).

Speaking about the airline's growth strategy, Hồ Ngọc Yến Phương, Vietjet's vice chairwoman and chief financial officer, said the company was focusing on improving operational efficiency while expanding its international route network.
She said Vietjet's hybrid airline model enabled it to expand connectivity while offering passengers a wider range of services at competitive prices.
Investments in fleet expansion, technology and workforce training were also key to strengthening its operational capabilities and service quality.

In the first nine months of 2026, Vietjet posted consolidated revenue of nearly VNĐ74.4 trillion (approximately US$2.9 billion), up 41 per cent year-on-year, equivalent to 86 per cent of its full-year target.
Consolidated profit after tax reached VNĐ1.72 trillion, meeting 82 per cent of the annual target.
The airline carried more than 20.7 million passengers during the period.
Vietjet has also expanded its international network, launching services to Almaty in Kazakhstan, Prague in the Czech Republic and Colombo in Sri Lanka, as well as routes connecting to the Maldives.
The airline is continuing to invest in next-generation aircraft, technology and its broader aviation ecosystem to improve operational efficiency and service quality.

Vietjet has previously been included in Việt Nam's Top 50 best-listed companies in 2026 and received international industry awards, including World's Best Ultra Low-Cost Carrier and Best Airline Financial Management.
The airline said the recognitions supported its ambition to develop into an international aviation group. -VNS
